belief: I'll end up just like my parent.
origins: Seeing a parent struggle with addiction, anger, depression, or illness, we may be terrified of repeating their path. Others tell us, “You’re just like your father,” and we may start acting as if the script is already written.
teaches: “The soul who sins is the one who will die. A son will not bear the iniquity of his father, and a father will not bear the iniquity of his son.” “Therefore if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation. The old has passed away. Behold, the new has come!” (2 Corinthians 5:17). “Do not be conformed to this world, but be transformed by the renewing of your mind” (Romans 12:2). You can learn from a parent’s pain what to avoid. Your life is your own to live with God’s help.
self_statements: I will make the same mistakes.
People expect me to turn out like them.
I am destined to repeat it.
errors: Believing I am either unlike my parent or identical.
Predicting that I will repeat their life.
Feeling the pull and concluding it is inevitable.
questions: In what ways am I different from my parent?
What did my parent lack that I can have?
What exactly do I fear repeating?
What choices can I make differently?
Who could support me, like a counselor, mentor, or pastor?
What does Scripture say about being a new creation?
truth: I am not my parent. I am a new creation in Christ, and I can choose differently, learn from their story, and receive support. My life is not a repeat.
hw_truths: The son does not bear the father’s iniquity.
God has a future for me.
log: Each week, note one choice that differs from the pattern.
actions: Write how you are not like your parent.
Write what you want to avoid.
prayer: Father, I fear repeating the past. Make me new, give me wisdom to choose differently, and surround me with support. Amen.
